title: Unable to access /userinfo endpoint when access token does not contain PII
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
We have created an issue in Pivotal Tracker to manage this: 

https://www.pivotaltracker.com/story/show/130370565 

The labels on this github issue will be updated when the story is started.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body: Hello @fhanik . Do you have any advice about how to deal with this issue ?

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body: @s-bortolussi it's a bug. email is a required claim, I'm fixing it right now.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
Thanks @fhanik for the fix.
However, I am wondering if it would not make more sense to use a more standard claim such as ["sub"](http://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#SubjectIDTypes) to represent user id instead of the non standard "user_id" claim.

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body:
@s-bortolussi `sub` is the subject. in case of client credentials, this should be the `client_id`. 
we use the presence of `user_id` to  tell us if it is a user token or not.
